body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, div outputs end furthest from full precision: microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition keeps only -inf dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) there with every tensor in its best format (fp8_e3m4 for this one); a node's SQNR counts the error accumulated along the data path up to it, not its own format's alone. Measured on 37 models with a format search (of 666 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 22.1 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst -2.4 dB (Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B). 23 of 31 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (token agreement 100% → 0%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's), openai/whisper-base (token agreement 100% → 0%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's) and microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (agreement 100% → 0%: the share of samples whose predicted class matches full precision's).

The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), linear in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors (fp8_e3m4, -19.0 dB), bmm in Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (fp8_e2m5, -14.0 dB), linear in Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (fp8_e2m5, -13.8 dB), linear in EleutherAI/pythia-160m (fp8_e3m4, -12.1 dB), linear in Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (fp8_e2m5, -12.0 dB), bmm in Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (fp8_e2m5, -10.3 dB), linear in Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (fp8_e2m5, -9.7 dB), relu in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors (fp8_e3m4, -8.9 dB) and bmm in EleutherAI/pythia-160m (fp8_e3m4, -8.6 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 11665 (48%), fp8_e3m4 9729 (40%), fp8_e1m6 2737 (11%), ufp8_e2m6 273 (1.11%), ufp8_e1m7 126 (0.51%), ufp8_e3m5 24 (0.10%), fp8_e4m3 1 (under 0.01%); 1.72% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where the most data carries the most error: div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB) and div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB).

body:
6 missing capabilities keep 37 operations in 14 models (of 33 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (18 operations in 9 models). Ranked by the MACs they hold:

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding and gather) needs a workaround. It affects 18 operations in 9 models: 18 calls (0.16% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in BAAI/bge-reranker-large, embedding in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions and embedding in Arunavaonly/Bangla-twoclass-Sentiment-Analyzer. Cost today: 0 of 18 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 18 wait for one; 362 workarounds proposed, 173 passing its check, 120 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**An upsample instruction.** The chip has no instruction for upsample, so every upsample needs a workaround. It affects 11 operations in 3 models: 11 calls (0.10% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: upsample in mattmdjaga/segformer_b2_clothes, upsample in nvidia/segformer-b2-finetuned-ade-512-512 and upsample in nvidia/segformer-b0-finetuned-ade-512-512. Cost today: 0 of 11 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 3 failed and 8 wait for one; 87 workarounds proposed, 18 passing its check, 4 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**A cumsum instruction.** The chip has no instruction for cumsum, so every cumsum needs a workaround. It affects 3 operations in 3 models: 3 calls (0.03% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: cumsum in BAAI/bge-reranker-large, cumsum in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions and cumsum in Arunavaonly/Bangla-twoclass-Sentiment-Analyzer. title: Missing instructions: 37 operations in 14 models need workarounds

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 895 of 2087 tensors passed between kernels (43%) in 29 models: 522 for attention heads split or merged, 334 for other reshapes, 19 for dimensions merged, 17 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 710 operations (710 calls, 6.19% of all calls; 176 G MACs, 3.74% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 215, linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207 and linear → add (other reshapes) 86; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (224), Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (137) and stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (129).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 895 of 2087 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 2,629 operations in 31 models (2,629 calls, 23% of all calls), most often layernorm (771), softmax (429) and silu (392). Their quantized accuracy: worst -inf dB SQNR over 2,142 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 14, most 65 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 65 planned groups), over 33 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.1 powers of ten for bmm in Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (largest value 2.75e+05).

286 outputs in 12 models hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (262), select_where (21) and amin (2), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

4 accuracy runs produced non-finite outputs (overflow or NaN).

Instruction memory (IMEM, 1,024 words per bank) use: not measured yet (no kernel built).
title: Resource limits: 2,629 operations limited by the LUT and up to 65 kernel launches per pass

body: The IPU architecture's costs, most costly first: **Resource limits** are the widest cost — 2,629 operations in 31 models (23% of all calls, mostly layernorm, softmax and silu) are constrained by a 256-entry LUT, with a worst case of -inf dB SQNR, and kernel launches reach a median of 14 and up to 65 per pass, while 286 outputs sit at the FP32 limit and 4 runs produced non-finite outputs. **Layout conversions** hit 895 of 2,087 inter-kernel tensors (43%) in 29 models, forcing reading kernels to rearrange data themselves (mostly attention head splits/merges after linear), affecting 710 calls and 176 G MACs, though cycles are not yet measured. **Missing instructions** keep 37 operations in 14 models off the chip's direct path, led by run-time addressing (18 operations, mostly embeddings) and upsample (11 operations), with only cumsum having a working workaround and none of the others having any workaround at all. **NX8 format quantization** is the most damaging where it bites: model outputs keep a median 22.1 dB SQNR but the worst is -2.4 dB, 23 of 31 models with a prediction metric lose some of it (three dropping to 0% agreement), and div in table-transformer-structure-recognition is worst at -inf dB; fp8_e2m5 and fp8_e3m4 dominate the chosen formats. **Compute efficiency** remains entirely unmeasured — no kernel has run, so MAC utilisation, cycles, IMEM use and accuracy for most workarounds are all unknown.
title: GLM summary

body:
**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip)** would put 18 operations in 9 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 18 calls (0.16% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**An upsample instruction** would put 11 operations in 3 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 11 calls (0.10% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**A cumsum instruction** would put 3 operations in 3 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 3 calls (0.03% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); recovering 0.00 dB of model output SQNR measured on 3 workarounds.

**An aten::type_as instruction** would put 3 operations in 3 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 3 calls (0.03% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**An aten::conv1d instruction** would put 1 operation in 1 model on the chip directly, with no workaround: 1 call (under 0.01% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**An aten::einsum instruction** would put 1 operation in 1 model on the chip directly, with no workaround: 1 call (under 0.01% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).
